snip.t: Treat statins and aspirin by overall cardiovascular risk, not blood pressure alone.

Prevent complications: infection (pneumococcal vaccine, prompt antibiotics for peritonitis), venous thrombosis (loss of antithrombin in the urine: consider anticoagulation in high-risk patients), hyperlipidaemia (statin), acute kidney injury.

qs.q: During the evaluation of a patient presenting with acute chest pain, statin therapy is initiated. While statins are recommended for everyone with ACS, they are particularly beneficial for patients with which lipid profile threshold?
qs.e: Statins are lipid-controlling agents given to everyone with ACS, but they are especially beneficial in patients with an LDL level greater than 100 mg/dL. They form a key component of the medical management regimen.

qs.q: A patient presents with an ALT elevation between 2 to 5 times normal. What is the recommended management regarding statin therapy?
o: Reduce the statin dose by half
Continue statins and monitor LFTs monthly
Switch to a non-statin lipid-lowering agent
qs.e: For mild ALT/AST elevations of 2 to 5 times normal, patients should continue statins while monitoring their LFTs monthly. Discontinuing statins unnecessarily interrupts beneficial cardiovascular risk reduction when only mild enzyme changes are present.

qs.q: A patient with mild ALT and AST elevations between 2-5 times the upper limit of normal is advised on lifestyle modifications and has hepatotoxic drugs discontinued. If statins are currently part of their regimen, what is the recommended management?
o: Reduce the statin dose by half
Continue statins and monitor LFTs monthly
Switch to a different lipid-lowering agent
qs.e: Statins can be continued while monitoring LFTs monthly in patients with mild elevations, alongside pursuing lifestyle changes. Immediate discontinuation is not mandated for mild elevations unless more severe injury develops.

qs.q: Which statin is commonly used to lower LDL cholesterol?
qs.e: ** Atorvastatin is a statin (HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor) that is the primary treatment for lowering LDL cholesterol. Other statins include simvastatin and rosuvastatin.
